title: Treat chronic hepatitis D with an authorized HDV-targeted antiviral

concept.text: Suppress HDV replication and improve liver inflammation using treatment directed at HDV infection. Bulevirtide achieved European authorization, but ongoing treatment should not be represented as a finite cure. Proposed completion test: European Commission marketing authorization following EMA assessment of virological and biochemical response in HDV-RNA-positive patients with compensated liver disease. Test set by: EMA and the European Commission; the clinical programme measures HDV RNA response and ALT normalization. Reported achieved: Hepcludex (bulevirtide) received EU conditional marketing authorization on 31 July 2020, converted to standard authorization on 18 July 2023. Overlaps: INF-11, VIR-03. Sources given: [EMA Hepcludex assessment and authorization history](https://www.ema.europa.eu/de/medicines/human/EPAR/hepcludex) ; [Hepcludex product information](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/hepcludex-epar-product-information_en.pdf).

page.title: EU-authorised antiviral treatment of chronic hepatitis D
page.definition: An antiviral medicine has EU-wide authorisation to treat chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection. HDV copies its RNA in liver cells and uses hepatitis B virus envelope proteins to form infectious particles. The first such medicine, bulevirtide, is authorised for adults and for children aged at least 3 years who weigh at least 10 kg. Patients must have detectable HDV RNA in blood and compensated liver disease, meaning their damaged liver still functions.

goal.need: An estimated 12 million people worldwide have HDV as well as chronic hepatitis B. Coinfection accelerates liver scarring and progression to cirrhosis. Hepatitis B nucleoside analogues have no direct effect on HDV. Pegylated interferon α can suppress HDV, but adverse effects and contraindications limit its use, and relapse is frequent. An alternative can reduce liver inflammation in people who cannot take interferon, with the aim of preventing liver failure. Maintaining viral suppression may require continued treatment.

completion.title: The European Commission authorises an antiviral for treatment of chronic hepatitis D throughout the EU.
completion.criterion: The European Commission grants at least one antiviral medicine a marketing authorisation valid throughout the EU whose approved therapeutic indications include treatment of chronic HDV infection. Either a conditional or a standard marketing authorisation qualifies.
completion.set_by: European Commission under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, Articles 10, 13 and 14-a.
completion.threshold_quote: throughout the EU on the basis of a single marketing authorisation.
completion.basis: The first grant was Commission Decision C(2020) 5426 of 31 July 2020 for Hepcludex (bulevirtide) in HDV-RNA-positive adults with compensated liver disease. The decision was conditional. In MYR202, 15 of 28 patients receiving 2 mg bulevirtide plus tenofovir had a virological response at week 24, compared with 1 of 28 receiving tenofovir alone. Standard authorisation followed in July 2023. In MYR301, 22 of 49 patients receiving 2 mg bulevirtide and 1 of 51 assigned to delayed treatment had both a virological response and normal alanine aminotransferase at week 48.

milestones.title: An HDV antiviral shows laboratory activity and has nonclinical safety evidence supporting human exposure.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical studies demonstrate the intended pharmacological action and characterize adverse effects sufficiently for the proposed human exposure. EMA reports bulevirtide inhibition of infection in human liver cells and mice with human hepatocytes. Cellular half-maximal inhibitory concentrations across HBV genotypes and HDV isolates were 14.5–834.0 pM. EMA considered the repeat-dose toxicity studies sufficient under ICH S6(R1). These measured concentrations are results, rather than a prescribed potency cutoff.
milestones.set_by: ICH M3(R2), section 1.4, sets the general nonclinical adequacy criterion; EMA assessed bulevirtide's peptide toxicology under ICH S6(R1).
milestones.threshold_quote: should be adequate to characterise potential adverse effects that might occur under the conditions of the clinical trial to be supported.

milestones.title: HDV RNA falls from baseline to week 24 on bulevirtide alone at two-tailed p < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: In the 2 mg/day bulevirtide monotherapy group of the MYR201 pilot substudy, mean log-transformed HDV RNA at week 24 is below baseline among participants with measurable baseline HDV RNA. The within-group comparison meets the published two-tailed p < 0.05 threshold after correction for multiple comparisons.
milestones.set_by: Myr GmbH and Centrosoyuz Clinical Hospital investigators, NCT02637999; secondary endpoint and statistical analysis published by Bogomolov and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: two-tailed p value <0.05 was considered significant.

milestones.title: Adding bulevirtide to tenofovir clears MYR202’s 5-point margin for week-24 HDV RNA response.
milestones.criterion: At week 24, response means undetectable serum HDV RNA or a fall of at least 2 log10 IU/mL from baseline. Compare each bulevirtide dose plus tenofovir with tenofovir alone among randomised participants who received at least one dose. Superiority requires rejecting the null that the response-rate difference is at most 5 percentage points, using a one-sided Wald test with Holm adjustment across the three comparisons at an overall significance level of 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Hepatera LLC, MYR202 protocol version 3.0, sections 9.1 and 9.2, and the statistical analysis documented in the CHMP assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: Treatment arms will be compared using the Wald test for Superiority by Margin of 5%

milestones.title: The CHMP recommends EU authorisation of an antiviral for chronic hepatitis D.
milestones.criterion: EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use adopts a favourable scientific opinion recommending marketing authorisation for a chronic HDV treatment indication. The proposed summary of product characteristics accompanying the opinion includes that indication.
milestones.set_by: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, under Article 9(4) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004.
milestones.threshold_quote: If an opinion is favourable to the granting of the relevant authorisation to place the medicinal product concerned on the market

milestones.title: A human study establishes tolerability across the antiviral dose range proposed for patient trials.
milestones.criterion: An initial human pharmacology study characterises adverse reactions and tolerability at exposures covering the dose range proposed for subsequent clinical studies.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, E8(R1), section 4.3.1.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: determine the tolerability of the dose range expected to be evaluated in later clinical studies

milestones.title: A candidate antiviral shows activity against HDV in a laboratory model.
milestones.criterion: A primary pharmacodynamic study demonstrates the candidate’s intended antiviral effect in an in vitro or in vivo model relevant to HDV.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, M3(R2), section 2 on primary pharmacodynamic studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: effects of a substance in relation to its desired therapeutic target.

milestones.title: Nonclinical safety data support the dose and duration of the first human HDV antiviral study.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical studies characterise potential adverse effects at the proposed human exposure sufficiently to support the starting dose, dose range and safety monitoring for the intended trial.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, M3(R2), section 1.4. The CHMP assessed bulevirtide’s peptide toxicology under ICH S6(R1).
milestones.threshold_quote: should be adequate to characterise potential adverse effects that might occur under the conditions of the clinical trial to be supported.

milestones.title: The Member States’ standing committee gives its opinion on the draft HDV authorisation decision.
milestones.criterion: After the CHMP opinion, the Commission submits its draft implementing decision to the Standing Committee on Medicinal Products for Human Use and obtains the committee’s opinion before adopting the final decision.
milestones.set_by: European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, Article 10(2).
milestones.threshold_quote: after obtaining the opinion of the Standing Committee on Medicinal Products for Human Use.

not_found: No HDV-specific numerical preclinical potency cutoff was found in searches of EMA assessments, ICH guidance and HDV antiviral-development literature.

results.finding: In the bulevirtide monotherapy arm (n = 7 evaluable), mean log-transformed HDV RNA fell from baseline to week 24 (p = 0.002).
results.detail: One of the eight participants in the monotherapy arm had no measurable baseline HDV RNA in the central laboratory.
results.quote:
Mean change from base-
line was a reduction of 10 1.67 copies/ml ( p = 0.002).

results.finding: The pilot bulevirtide dose was about 90-fold below the rat and dog no-observed-effect level on a mg/kg basis. Animal sample sizes were unreported.
results.detail: The ratio compares doses by body weight. The authors chose the 24-week course to assess preliminary efficacy while limiting exposure.
results.quote:
This dose was approximately 90 times lower than the dose, which
was deﬁned as the ‘no observed effect level’ (NOEL) of 2.5 mg/kg in both rat
and dog (i.e., 2 mg/70 kg resulting in /C240.028 mg/kg).

results.finding: Among 118 adults, the pooled six-month HDV RNA response rate was 57.5 percentage points higher with bulevirtide plus tenofovir than with tenofovir alone.
results.detail: The 57.5-point difference is calculated from the reported counts. The excerpt gives no dose-specific estimates or test results.
results.quote: In the first study, 55 out of 90 patients treated with Hepcludex plus tenofovir (a medicine for hepatitis B) had substantial reductions in HDV replication after 6 months, compared with 1 out of 28 patients given tenofovir alone.

results.finding: EMA first published the adopted CHMP positive opinion for Hepcludex on 29 May 2020.
results.detail: The date is the publication date. This regulatory action has no sample size.

results.finding: Hepcludex received EU-wide conditional marketing authorisation for chronic HDV treatment on 31 July 2020.
results.detail: The current indication covers adults and children aged at least 3 years and weighing at least 10 kg with detectable HDV RNA and compensated liver disease. This regulatory action has no sample size.
results.quote: Hepcludex received a conditional marketing authorisation valid throughout the EU on 31 July 2020.

results.finding: Bulevirtide inhibited HDV infection in primary human hepatocytes (n = 57 evaluable genotype combinations), with mean EC50 values of 0.44–0.64 nM across HDV genotypes.
results.detail: The study measured HDV antigen-positive cells five days after inoculation. Seven of the 64 genotype combinations yielded no measurable antigen signal, so their EC50 values could not be determined.
results.quote: The mean BLV EC 50 against HDV laboratory strains ranged from 0.44 to 0.64 nM.

results.finding: In repeat-dose bulevirtide studies (80 rats in the 26-week study and 24 treated dogs), the no-observed-adverse-effect level was 2.5 mg/kg/day in both species.
results.detail: CHMP judged the repeat-dose studies sufficient for the marketing assessment. The early clinical study descriptions give doses and some measurements, but provide no trial-specific rationale linking the nonclinical findings to those choices.
results.quote:
Thus, the NOAEL was set at 
2.5 mg/kg in both rats and dogs corresponding to AUC exposure margins of >30 in rats and >60 in dogs.

results.finding: Myrcludex B was well tolerated in 36 healthy volunteers at single intravenous doses up to 20 mg.
results.detail: The report reproduces the published phase I abstract, which establishes the reported tolerability finding. Coverage of the proposed patient-trial exposures remains unverified.
results.quote:
The project TTU 05.901 
comprised the continuation of a “first in man” (FIM) study, which revealed Myrcludex B to be 
safe and well tolerated in 36 healthy volunteers up to single doses of 20 mg IV.

results.finding: For one product, Hepcludex (bulevirtide), the 31 July 2020 decision records agreement with the Standing Committee’s opinion.
results.detail: Recital 6 records the committee’s opinion. The draft referral and its timing relative to the CHMP opinion are undocumented in the supplied text.
results.quote:
The measures provided for in this Decision are in accordance with the opinion of the 
Standing Committee on Medicinal Products for Human Use,

definition = "An antiviral medicine has EU-wide authorisation to treat chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection. HDV copies its RNA in liver cells and uses hepatitis B virus envelope proteins to form infectious particles. The first such medicine, bulevirtide, is authorised for adults and for children aged at least 3 years who weigh at least 10 kg. Patients must have detectable HDV RNA in blood and compensated liver disease, meaning their damaged liver still functions.". Reason: The definition conflates HDV RNA replication with its dependence on HBV for infectious particles and describes only the original adult indication.

goal.need = "An estimated 12 million people worldwide have HDV as well as chronic hepatitis B. Coinfection accelerates liver scarring and progression to cirrhosis. Hepatitis B nucleoside analogues have no direct effect on HDV. Pegylated interferon \u03b1 can suppress HDV, but adverse effects and contraindications limit its use, and relapse is frequent. An alternative can reduce liver inflammation in people who cannot take interferon, with the aim of preventing liver failure. Maintaining viral suppression may require continued treatment.". Reason: The existing need gives prevalence and treatment limitations but omits what suppressing HDV could change for patients and how long suppression may require treatment.

add statement by European Commission, 2015: "Treatment of hepatitis delta virus infection". Reason: The 2015 orphan designation identifies treatment of HDV as a development goal five years before the first EU authorisation.
